correctness.rationale: The four-cycle through r proves strong connectivity on the same seven positive arcs for every z>0. Of the eight nonroot parent assignments, two close b↔x and one closes b→x→y→b. The five remaining assignments (parents of b,x,y in that order) are (r,b,r), (r,b,b), (r,y,r), (r,y,b), (x,y,r), of weights z²,z³,z,z²,1. The second alone has off-diagonal LCA b; the first, second and fourth contribute to x's ancestor probability, and the second and fourth to y's. Thus with Z=1+z+2z²+z³ the probabilities Hx,Hy,a are z²(z+2)/Z,z²(z+1)/Z,z³/Z. The stated law gives f(x)Hx=f(y)Hy and the diagonal LCA events are zero, so the iid ratio is a/(2HxHy)=Z/[2z(z+1)(z+2)]. Its small-z divergence is 1/(4z); subtracting the denominator from the numerator gives 1−3z−4z²−z³, strictly decreasing from 1 to −∞. Exact substitution at 1/8 gives Hx=17/593, Hy=9/593, a=1/593, and ratio 593/306. All identities follow from the complete symbolic enumeration; the frozen seventeen-parameter checker was inspected, not run or relied on.
